component.name: SRS System Information
component.summary: Show what is inside your PC and whether it is healthy

description.p: SRS is a system information viewer for Linux. It shows the processor, memory, motherboard and BIOS, graphics and audio, drives, network, sensors, USB and PCI devices and the operating system, in plain words first and with every detail one click away.

The Overview answers "Is my PC OK?": temperatures judged against each sensor's own limit, drive health (SMART), hardware errors, free disk space and memory in use, each with a status light and an explanation.

SRS is inspired by SIV (System Information Viewer) by Ray Hinchliffe, RH Software. It is an independent project, not affiliated with SIV or its author, and contains no SIV code or data. A classic view with SIV-style windows is included.

The GPU tests run through Vulkan, ROCm / HIP, CUDA (also ZLUDA on AMD cards, with SRS's built-in CUDA kernels) and OpenCL. The NVIDIA CUDA toolkit is optional; SRS explains what it is for and can install it later from its Options menu.

ul.li: Stress tests and benchmarks are used at your own risk: SRS is provided without warranty and asks you to agree once before the first one

CPU and GPU burn-in and stress tests in one Stress & Burnin window; Dhrystone, Whetstone, Cache & Memory, Storage, OS Latency, CPU Compute, Everyday Work, Network, GPU, GPU Compute comparison (Vulkan, ROCm/HIP, CUDA, OpenCL), SRS Pi, Crypto and Prime Sieve benchmarks and a memory latency test
Power & Cost: an estimate of the whole PC's power use and its cost, with recorded history (estimates, not a meter reading)
Tabs you can arrange and save as lineups, sortable tables and a startup manager
Device ID lookup for PCI and USB devices
Reports saved as text, and a command-line report search
Optional root-only details (DMI, memory SPD, SMART, MSRs) collected with one password prompt
A built-in user guide: F1 opens it at the section for the item you are looking at

screenshot.caption: The main window with the Overview page
The sensors panel in the classic view

description.p: Stress & Burnin: CPU Burnin, CPU Stress and GPU Burnin in one window, the GPU load for its own time or in sync with the CPU load, a custom GPU command as the other choice. In the new main window every benchmark and stress test is a tab of the Benchmarks & Stress page.

Use at your own risk: the first stress test or benchmark asks you to agree to plain-English terms (provided as is, without warranty). Columns now line up on every page; very long entries end in "..." with the full text in the tooltip and in Copy.

Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT): the built-in GPU Burnin in Stress & Burnin was tested on a software renderer only; parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two - please report them.

CUDA without the NVIDIA runtime compiler: SRS's CUDA test kernels are now built in (pre-compiled PTX), so GPU Burnin and every CUDA row of the GPU Compute comparison run with ZLUDA on AMD cards too. OpenCL drivers without double precision now say "not available" with the reason instead of "failed".

The NVIDIA CUDA toolkit is explained and optional: SRS asks once before the first CUDA run when it is missing, and it can be installed later from Options; with ZLUDA, SRS warns that installing it can break or remove ZLUDA.

Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT, wired connection): parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two; the built-in CUDA kernels were never run on NVIDIA hardware. Please report problems on GitHub Issues.

Fix: GPU Comparison and GPU Burnin no longer crash when the vendor GEMM library (hipBLAS or cuBLAS) is measured before the own kernels; a missing runtime compiler is now reported with a clear message.
Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT, wired connection): parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two. Please report them on GitHub Issues.

Fixes: clear messages after a hung GPU driver call and when CPU Burnin cannot start, an honest All GPUs verdict in GPU Burnin when one card cannot start, a safer CPU/GPU burn-in start check on ARM, and a default window size that fits the screen.
Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT, wired connection): parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two. Please report them on GitHub Issues.

A Power & cost page that estimates the whole PC's power use and what it costs, with history, sessions, alarms and offline price tables. New benchmarks: Cache & Memory, Storage, OS Latency, CPU Compute, Everyday Work, Network, GPU Benchmark, GPU Burnin, GPU Compute comparison, SRS Pi, Crypto and Prime Sieve, with a run history; each asks before it starts. Tabs you can arrange and save as lineups, sortable tables, a Startup manager that turns startup items off and on without deleting anything, a Full access / Limited badge, and stock-versus-in-effect clocks on CPU Clocks.
Tested on one PC (Ryzen 7 7800X3D, Radeon RX 9070 XT, wired connection): parts that need other hardware may have a bug or two. Please report them on GitHub Issues.

A new main window with an Overview that answers "Is my PC OK?", one page per category, search, and an AppImage for any distribution that can update itself. The classic SIV-style windows are still available.
